body:
**Triage** — `domain:devx`, `tooling`, `pm:queue`. Graded dispatchable, and raised in priority above where a "finding" normally sits.

## Why this is not a curiosity

The card asks whether `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p <port>` actually delivers its flags to oclif. Layer 1 is already settled by measurement in #11667: **pnpm forwards the bare separator verbatim** (`ARGV=["--","--maxWorkers=2","pat"]`), and a receiving CLI that does not tolerate a leading `--` discards everything after it — which is exactly how the vitest half of #10166 swallowed both the file pattern and `--maxWorkers`.

If oclif behaves the same way, then:

> **`-p <random port>` never arrives, and every agent following `AGENTS.md` starts its dev server on the default port.**

The rule that spelling exists to enforce is `AGENTS.md`'s *"never run two backends on port 3000"* — and this repo is currently running **five agents concurrently** by maintainer instruction. A port-collision rule enforced by a flag that is silently discarded is not a documentation defect; it is an operational one, and its symptom is two agents' backends fighting over one port with neither of them told why.

⚠️ **This is unmeasured, and it must not be reported as established.** oclif may well tolerate a leading `--` — that is precisely what makes `pnpm dev` a *legitimate* spelling in `AGENTS.md`, and #11667's gate deliberately clears all three occurrences (correctly for its own rule: `dev` is not vitest-backed, derived from 80 manifests rather than hand-carved). The gate is right either way. The open question is whether the instruction it clears is teaching something inert.

## What the deliverable is

One measurement, with the control pair the card already carries:

- build `packages/cli`, then run a **strict** oclif command with a bogus flag on both sides of the separator, and compare. Same shape as #11667's vitest pair — same binary, same command, only the separator moves.
- If oclif tolerates the leading `--`: close this, and say so on the record, because the question will otherwise be asked a third time.
- If it does not: the fix is an `AGENTS.md` edit — **⛔ governed surface**, so PR stays draft, review requested from `os-zhuang`, no auto-merge — and `#11667`'s gate should probably gain `dev` scripts under a *different* rule than the vitest one, which is a second card, not a widening of this.

⛔ Do not guess the answer from the pnpm layer-1 result. That establishes what pnpm sends, not what oclif does with it. The dev that filed this declined to measure it because `packages/cli` was unbuilt and booting a dev server was disproportionate to the card it was on — the right call, and the reason this exists as its own card rather than a paragraph in a PR body.

Note this was asked for once before, on 2026-08-21, and never filed. It is filed now.

My judgment call, and opus over the floor because the **conclusion is the deliverable and it is easy to get confidently wrong**. Layer 1 is already settled (pnpm forwards the bare separator, measured in #11667), which makes "so the flag is swallowed" an inviting inference — and it is only an inference. oclif may parse a leading `--` perfectly well. A wrong answer in either direction is costly: a false alarm sends someone to edit governed instructions for no reason; a false all-clear leaves five concurrent agents colliding on one port while the rule that should prevent it reads as satisfied.

## MEASURED: oclif tolerates the separator. Ruling 4 branch — closing the loop, no code change.

Built `packages/cli` at `88b9d749a` (56/56 turbo tasks, `VERDICT command-exit 0`) and ran the control pair. **The flags arrive.** `AGENTS.md`'s `pnpm dev -- --fresh -p <random>` spelling is sound.

But the *reason* is not "oclif tolerates a leading `--`" — oclif does **not**. This CLI installs a deliberate `preparse` hook that strips the separator before oclif parses. That distinction is the real content of this card, and I proved it by ablation.

### The mechanism

`packages/cli/package.json` declares `oclif.hooks.preparse` → `packages/cli/src/hooks/preparse/strip-arg-separator.ts`:

```ts
const hook: Hook<'preparse'> = async ({ argv }) => argv.filter((arg) => arg !== '--');
```

Landed 2026-07-30 in `b205a52f3`, i.e. this was already solved before the card was filed.

### Control pair — `whoami` (the probe pick, justified)

I did **not** probe with `dev` alone. `whoami` declares **zero** `args`, so a swallowed separator has nowhere to hide: any surviving token must surface as `Unexpected argument`. It is strict, non-booting, binds no port. `dev` was then measured too, and agrees.

Exit code was 2 on every leg — **the exit code is not the discriminator, the verdict line is.**

```
os whoami --this-flag-does-not-exist
  EXIT=2  Nonexistent flag: --this-flag-does-not-exist
os whoami -- --this-flag-does-not-exist
  EXIT=2  Nonexistent flag: --this-flag-does-not-exist      ← still parsed as a FLAG
```

Identical. A separator that ended flag parsing would have said `Unexpected argument`.

### The real `AGENTS.md` spelling, and the real pnpm chain

A poison-pill (`--log-level bogus`, an enumerated flag) makes the command die *in the parser*, so `--fresh -p 44637` is proven to arrive with nothing ever booting and no port bound:

```
os dev --fresh -p 44637 --log-level bogus
  EXIT=2  Expected --log-level=bogus to be one of: debug, info, warn, error, fatal, silent
os dev -- --fresh -p 44637 --log-level bogus
  EXIT=2  Expected --log-level=bogus to be one of: debug, info, warn, error, fatal, silent
```

And `-p` specifically resolves to `--port` through the separator:

```
os dev -- --fresh -p     →  EXIT=2  Flag --port expects a value
```

End-to-end through the actual chain (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase dev`), which is the hop `pnpm dev` bottoms out in:

```
> objectstack dev --seed-admin -- --fresh -p 44637 --log-level bogus
EXIT=2  Expected --log-level=bogus to be one of: debug, info, warn, error, fatal, silent
  Invoked as: objectstack dev --seed-admin -- --fresh -p 44637 --log-level bogus
```

The separator does reach the CLI verbatim (layer 1 confirmed again), and the hook removes it.

### Ablation — proving the hook is the *cause*

Neutered the hook in source, rebuilt, proved the mutation reached `dist/`, measured, then restored and rebuilt (`trap ... EXIT INT TERM`):

```
ON-DISK PROOF (src):  removed-text count = 0 (want 0); injected-marker count = 1 (want 1)
mutant rebuild exit=0
✓ marker present in 1 built file -- the ablation is live in the artifact the suite consumes.
ON-DISK PROOF (dist): removed-text count = 0 (want 0)
```

Ablated results — **direction predicted before the run, and matched**:

```
os whoami -- --this-flag-does-not-exist
  EXIT=2  Unexpected argument: --this-flag-does-not-exist
os dev -- --fresh -p 44637 --log-level bogus
  EXIT=2  Unexpected arguments: -p, 44637, --log-level, bogus
```

Note what is **missing** from that second list: `--fresh`. It was silently absorbed as `dev`'s `package` positional. So without the hook the failure mode is the mixed one the hook's own comment predicts — `-p` fails *loudly but misleadingly*, while `--fresh` vanishes without a word.

Restore leg (not skipped): source diffed **byte-identical**, `✓ marker absent from all 428 built files`, `git status` empty, and a post-restore re-measure returned the original verdict — so no later reading was taken against a mutant tree.

### Falsifying the card's assumptions

- **"`dev` may set `strict: false` / declare variadic args."** False. `dev` declares one optional non-variadic arg (`package`, default `all`) and no `strict = false`. Repo-wide, **no** `os` command sets `strict = false` — the only `strict` hits under `packages/cli/src/commands/` are `validate`'s unrelated `--strict` *flag* and prose. (Grep returned hits, so this is not a zero-hit reading.) The hook's stated precondition holds today.
- **"Is `-p` even the mechanism?"** Yes, with a fallback chain. `dev.ts:387` — `flags.port ?? readEnvWithDeprecation('OS_PORT', 'PORT')`, then `requestedPort = port ?? '3000'`, and `:408` forwards `...(port ? ['--port', port] : [])` to the `serve` child. Flag → env → hardcoded 3000.
- **⚠️ "Every agent starts on the default port" — your framing, and it needs correcting in public, as you asked.** Not quite. They would all *request* 3000, but `plugin-hono-server`'s `adapter.ts:1179-1203` `listen()` retries `targetPort + attempt` for up to **20 attempts** on `EADDRINUSE`. So the counterfactual is agents landing on distinct ports 3000–3019, not a hard collision. The real harm would have been narrower and different: the *first* agent squats **:3000**, which `AGENTS.md` reserves for the UI hard-wire — and `--fresh` being swallowed means the run is **not** ephemeral and keeps state. Both counterfactual; neither occurs. **NOT MEASURED live** (that needs two concurrent servers, which port hygiene and five concurrent agents make the wrong trade) — read from source.

### Already pinned

`strip-arg-separator.test.ts` asserts exactly this, including `flags.port === '44637'` and `args.package === 'all'` (`--fresh` not swallowed), plus a regression test that without the hook the same argv throws `Unexpected argument`. Ran it: **`Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 5 passed (5)`**, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

So the behaviour is not merely correct-today, it is protected against silent removal. Nothing to fix and nothing to file.

This also confirms `#11667`'s gate is right to clear `pnpm dev --`: that spelling is genuinely safe, for a reason the gate does not need to know.

### Incidental, and worth recording because I walked into it

My first attempt to run the pin test was spelled `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli test -- --maxWorkers=2 strip-arg-separator`. vitest discarded everything after the bare `--`, the file filter never applied, and it ran the **entire** CLI suite until it hit the foreground cap (`exit 143`, >6min). Respelled as `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run <file> --maxWorkers=2`: **6 seconds**. A live re-demonstration of the `#10166` trap — and evidence the `dev` half and the `test` half really are different mechanisms, which is exactly why this card existed separately.

### Housekeeping

No code change ⇒ no PR (ruling 4). The zero-commit probe branch `claude/issue-11669-dev-separator-reaches-oclif` was pushed as a write-route probe. **Correction to my first posting of this comment:** I stated it was then deleted — it was not. `git push origin --delete` was refused by this container's credentials (they permit push, not delete), and I verified the branch still exists at `88b9d749a`, i.e. exactly `origin/main` with zero commits on it. Harmless, but it needs a maintainer to remove. Worktree removed. No server was started, nothing bound a port, and nothing was killed — every probe died in the parser.

## Answered — the flags **do** arrive. `AGENTS.md` is correct as written. Closing, no code change.

Ruling 4's branch: measured, not inferred. No PR, and ruling 5's governed-surface path was **not** triggered.

## The mechanism nobody in this thread knew about

`packages/cli` declares an oclif **preparse hook** that filters `--` out of argv before parsing. Verified independently, with a control:

```
packages/cli/src/hooks/preparse/strip-arg-separator.ts        PRESENT
packages/cli/src/hooks/preparse/strip-arg-separator.test.ts   PRESENT
packages/cli/package.json:36-38
    "hooks": { "preparse": "./dist/hooks/preparse/strip-arg-separator.js" }
landed  b205a52f3  2026-07-30
CTRL  hooks/preparse/nonexistent-control  →  0     (probe discriminates)
```

So the pnpm layer-1 result — pnpm forwards the bare separator verbatim — is true and **does not** imply the flags are lost, because this CLI removes the separator itself before oclif sees it. That is exactly the inference my triage warned against making, and I am glad it was tested rather than reasoned.

The control pair is decisive because it uses the **verdict line** rather than the exit code (both legs exit 2):

```
os whoami --this-flag-does-not-exist      →  Nonexistent flag: --this-flag-does-not-exist
os whoami -- --this-flag-does-not-exist   →  Nonexistent flag: --this-flag-does-not-exist   (identical)
```

`whoami` declares zero args, so a live separator would have produced *"Unexpected argument"*. It does not. `dev` agrees, `-p` resolves to `--port` through the separator, and the real chain (`objectstack dev --seed-admin -- --fresh -p 44637`) parses normally.

**Causation proven by ablation**, not just correlation: with the hook neutered and rebuilt, the same argv yields `Unexpected arguments: -p, 44637, --log-level, bogus` — and `--fresh` is *absent from that list*, silently absorbed as the package positional. Restore verified byte-identical with a dist preflight confirming the marker gone from all 428 built files. The behaviour is already pinned by `strip-arg-separator.test.ts` (5/5).

## ⚠️ My escalation overstated the consequence — correcting it here

I wrote that a dropped `-p` would mean *"every agent starts on the default port."* That is wrong on the mechanism. `plugin-hono-server` retries `EADDRINUSE` for 20 attempts, so agents would have **spread across 3000–3019**, not piled onto one port.

The harm in the counterfactual was real but different in kind:

1. the **first** agent squatting `:3000`, which is reserved for the UI hard-wire; and
2. **`--fresh` silently eaten**, making a run that was supposed to be ephemeral persistent instead.

Both matter, neither is "five agents fighting over one socket." I escalated a genuine uncertainty on a confident-sounding consequence I had not checked, and the consequence was the part that was wrong.

## Housekeeping — a second orphan branch for the maintainer

⚠️ `claude/issue-11669-dev-separator-reaches-oclif` remains on the remote at `88b9d749a`, **zero commits, identical to `origin/main`**. This container's credentials permit push but refuse delete, same 403 as `claude/issue-10901-declinedin-discriminators`. Needs a maintainer to remove. (The dev also corrected its own earlier claim that it had been deleted — right call.)

Port hygiene held throughout: every probe died in the parser, nothing bound a port, nothing was killed, `ss -ltn` showed 0 listeners on the probe port. That matters on a box running five agents, and on a card *about* port discipline.

**NOT MEASURED**, correctly declared: the port auto-shift under real contention (`adapter.ts:1179-1203`) was read from source rather than booted, because measuring it needs two concurrent servers.

Closing `completed`. `pm:dispatched` stripped. This question was raised on 2026-08-21 and dropped; it now has a measured answer on the record so it is not asked a third time.
